name: Beijing Normal-Hong Kong Baptist University (formerly UIC)
summary: English-medium liberal-arts university in Zhuhai, formerly UIC, with 32 undergraduate programmes and some bilingual core activities.

ib.text: IB Diploma accepted; no aggregate floor located. Proposed English rules: A at 4 HL/SL, B at 4 HL or 5 SL, or Literature and Performance at 4 SL; IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL 79 also listed. Test validity explicitly covers 2027.

notes: Formerly known as UIC, the university is now BNBU. International applications are separate from Chinese mainland admission.
Teaching, assessment and examinations are in English except bilingual Whole Person Education and Healthy Lifestyle courses; confirm provision if you do not speak Chinese.
The fee page quotes RMB 110,000 a year but lacks a 2027 tuition label; its insurance/utilities and the scholarship policy still reference 2026.

programmes.name: Game Design
programmes.about: Combine interactive storytelling, programming, visual design and production skills to create digital games and related experiences.
programmes.overview: Students combine creative design with the technical processes used to make digital games. The programme covers game engines, game design, production and project management, with work involving virtual reality, motion capture and generative AI. Computer labs, production studios and elective study support practical exploration across computing and media arts. The curriculum combines major study with university core and general education, preparing students for game production, adjacent creative technology fields or further study.
programmes.ib: IB Diploma and recognised English evidence; some university-wide courses are bilingual. Confirm 2027 programme-specific subjects and any interview or portfolio.
programmes.selectionNote: International applications are reviewed using school results and interview performance; confirm whether this major has additional 2027 submission requirements.

programmes.name: Globalisation and Development
programmes.about: Investigate global development, public policy and international cooperation with social-science research and digital analytical methods.
programmes.overview: The degree connects political science, development economics and international relations with the study of sustainability and public policy. Published modules include research methods, social-science data analysis, digital transformation and environmental governance, alongside studies of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. In later years students can pursue International Development or Public Administration, subject to enrolment and the cohort curriculum. The programme includes a final-year project and presents research, policy and international-organisation work as potential pathways.
